subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experimental Claws remove policy—default retention of referenced resources with explicit selected and forced cleanup—as a public lifecycle contract for the stacked feature?
rationale: The implementation adds a new destructive lifecycle mode and shared package-ownership semantics; tests can verify mechanics but cannot choose the intended long-term operator and upgrade policy.

options.title: Sponsor the policy and require proof
options.body: Confirm the managed/referenced cleanup contract, then require exact-head live evidence for every cleanup mode before normal merge review.

options.title: Narrow to non-destructive removal
options.body: Retain only reference release and managed-state cleanup until a later maintainer-approved design defines selected referenced-resource removal.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the lifecycle slice until the RFC and package-owner semantics receive explicit maintainer resolution.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the policy and require proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the managed/referenced cleanup contract, then require exact-head live evidence for every cleanup mode before normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the stacked contract and can supply the requested evidence, though acceptance of the product direction must come from a repository maintainer.
